title: How Nvidia, Micron and a surprising jobs report drove last week's stock action
source_used: Stocktwits (CNBC original blocked, 403); IBD weekly review snippet; Bloomberg via Yahoo for yields context
key_facts: US stocks ended the week higher on Friday 2 Oct 2026: S&P 500 +0.7 percent to 7,722.72, Nasdaq 100 +1 percent to 30,807.93, Dow +0.5 percent to 51,176.96 (Stocktwits)
September payrolls rose only 29,000 against a Dow Jones consensus of 84,000 and unemployment rose to 4.2 percent; odds of an October Fed hike fell to 22 percent from 64 percent a week earlier
Chip stocks led: semiconductor ETFs rose about 2 percent on gains in Nvidia, Micron and AMD; Micron beat expectations on 30 Sep (Korea Herald)
The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.28 percent and the 30-year at 5.62 percent after touching 22-year highs earlier in the week (IBD, Bloomberg)
IBD says the Nasdaq hit a record high on Friday; SpaceX shares jumped on AI computing contracts
quote_evidence: U.S. stock indices ended higher on Friday as employment data showed the economy added fewer jobs than expected, easing fears of an October rate hike.
The probability of an October hike significantly dropped to 22% on Friday from 64% a week ago.
The stock market had a mixed week but with a bullish finish as Treasury yields retreated from 22-year highs, while crude oil prices tumbled. The Nasdaq rallied a record high on Friday.
why_it_matters_hint: A weak jobs report pushed back rate-hike fears and let AI chip stocks carry the market to a record
notes: CNBC original (Investing Club) blocked with 403; same weekly story read on Stocktwits (2 Oct) with IBD and Bloomberg for context. Market recap, no single new event.
